name: Rail Transport
description: Rail transport in Iran encompasses national railway infrastructure, passenger journeys, freight movements, and urban metro systems. Understanding these activities requires separating the physical network from the services using it and distinguishing historical railway heritage from contemporary operating performance.

seo.title: Rail Transport in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore Iran’s railway infrastructure, passenger services, freight, and railway heritage, with clear distinctions between networks and operations.

content.heading: A network, a service, and a historical landscape
content.content:
A railway can be understood through several different questions: where its tracks run, what trains use them, how much traffic they carry, and what buildings and engineering works survive from earlier periods. These perspectives are complementary, but their evidence is different. The International Union of Railways, generally known as UIC, separately records infrastructure, passenger traffic, freight traffic, train movements, and rolling stock. Its statistical framework provides a useful starting point for keeping these subjects distinct. [s1]

The Iranian railway story also has a substantial heritage dimension. UNESCO’s account of the Trans-Iranian Railway describes a historic line joining the Caspian Sea and Persian Gulf through markedly different landscapes. Its construction began in 1927 and finished in 1938. That historic corridor is an important part of Iran’s railway geography, but its dimensions should not be used as the size of the entire contemporary network. [s2]

content.heading: What infrastructure and traffic statistics explain
content.content:
Infrastructure statistics describe the railway available for use; traffic statistics describe activity on it. UIC distinguishes the length of lines from the length of tracks and reports passenger-kilometres and tonne-kilometres alongside other measures. A route with additional parallel tracks therefore requires a different interpretation from a newly connected destination. Likewise, the number of passenger journeys and the distance those passengers travel answer different questions. [s1]

Comparisons need particular care when the reporting organization or its activities change. UIC explicitly identifies corporate restructuring, subsidiaries, privatization, and differences in business scope as challenges for consistent railway statistics. An apparent national trend should therefore be checked against the coverage of the contributing railway companies before it is explained as a change in travel demand or infrastructure provision. [s1]

content.heading: Passenger services are more specific than a line on a map
content.content:
Passenger experience depends on the particular train and service offered. Fadak’s official website, for example, describes compartment accommodation, sleeping facilities, entertainment, and catering. These descriptions establish what this operator advertises; they are not independent measurements of comfort, punctuality, or customer satisfaction. They also should not be generalized to every Iranian passenger train. The undated website was inspected after this page’s research cutoff, so its exact offerings on the cutoff date remain unconfirmed. [s3]

A useful account of rail transport consequently needs both physical and operational evidence. A railway map can explain connections, while dated service information establishes which passenger journeys are actually offered. Performance data are needed for conclusions about reliability or effectiveness. This page currently provides the conceptual distinctions and historical foundation; a complete contemporary synthesis still requires verified operating and traffic evidence.

name: Iranian Rail Network
description: Iran’s railway network has a major historical foundation in the Trans-Iranian Railway, which linked the Caspian Sea with the Persian Gulf. Its mountain engineering and subsequent expansion help explain the distinction between a protected historical corridor and the wider national system.

seo.title: Iranian Rail Network: Geography and Engineering | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Understand the historical foundation of Iran’s railway network, its mountain engineering, and the limits of available contemporary network evidence.

content.heading: The historic north–south corridor
content.content:
The Trans-Iranian Railway extends for 1,394 kilometres between the Caspian Sea and Persian Gulf. UNESCO identifies its track gauge—the distance between the rails—as 1,435 millimetres, the gauge commonly called standard gauge. The corridor’s scale and engineering make it central to understanding Iran’s railway history, but it is not a measurement of the entire national network. [s1]

The International Council on Monuments and Sites, or ICOMOS, identifies the historic endpoints as Bandar-e Torkaman in the northeast and Bandar-e Imam Khomeini in the southwest. Its evaluation also records later railway expansion beginning in the 1940s and continuing after wartime interruption. The historical trunk and subsequent additions must therefore be distinguished when describing the network. [s2]

content.heading: Engineering across contrasting landscapes
content.content:
The historic railway crosses the Alborz and Zagros mountains as well as forests, plateau landscapes, and coastal regions. UNESCO records 224 tunnels, including 11 spiral tunnels, illustrating how the alignment negotiated difficult terrain. These structures explain the route’s engineering significance more directly than a simple line on a national map. [s1, s2]

For a network overview, the important distinction is between geographical reach and operational capability. A historic alignment establishes where infrastructure was built; it does not by itself establish present-day speeds, train frequency, available capacity, or disruption levels. Those questions require contemporary technical and operating records.

content.summary: A schematic of the historic corridor’s geographical sequence. Arrows indicate the order of places and landscapes along the route, not scheduled passenger services, distances, or travel times.

content.heading: A working railway and a conservation challenge
content.content:
ICOMOS’s 2020 evaluation describes the historic line as carrying passenger and freight traffic. It distinguishes maintained infrastructure still in use from redundant buildings and equipment needing conservation or reuse. This creates a practical heritage question: how can modernization preserve historically significant structures and machinery? [s2]

That assessment is dated evidence, not a current condition inspection. A complete account of the Iranian rail network still needs a verified contemporary map, consistent route-length definitions, and dated confirmation of individual openings and operating connections.

name: Intercity Trains
description: Intercity passenger rail is best understood through specific train services, accommodation, stopping patterns, and ticket conditions. Inspected operator documentation illustrates these distinctions, while leaving nationwide service coverage and performance unresolved.

seo.title: Intercity Trains in Iran: Services and Accommodation | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: An evidence-based introduction to Iranian intercity train accommodation, service information, and the distinction between advertised routes and dated availability.

content.heading: Read the service, not just the destination
content.content:
A city pair alone does not describe a passenger train. Accommodation, stopping pattern, catering, and ticket conditions also matter. Fadak’s official purchase guide illustrates this distinction: it directs users to separate information about train facilities, intermediate stations, and refund conditions within the booking results. This is evidence about the operator’s documented booking process, not a nationwide standard for every railway company. [s1]

The guide also distinguishes an ordinary compartment booking from reserving a whole compartment. For an international reader, the useful point is that a place on a train and exclusive use of a compartment are different products. The exact arrangement must be established from the selected service rather than inferred from the general appearance of a train. [s1]

content.heading: Accommodation and advertised amenities
content.content:
Fadak describes its trains in terms of compartment accommodation, beds, bedding, entertainment, internet access, and onboard hospitality. Its detailed introduction also describes compartment air conditioning and catering tables. These are operator descriptions of the product being sold. They do not independently establish that every amenity is available on every departure or that passengers consistently receive the advertised experience. [s2, s3]

The same distinction applies to bundled travel. Fadak describes packages combining rail tickets with hotels and, in some cases, transfers or other destination services. A transfer included in a particular package should not be treated as an automatic feature of a standalone rail ticket. [s3]

These undated pages were inspected after the requested cutoff. Their descriptions are useful evidence of what the website presented at inspection, but they cannot alone establish the precise product available on 26 October 2026.

content.heading: Advertised routes and dated availability
content.content:
Fadak’s homepage presents Tehran–Mashhad and connections involving Rasht among its prominent routes. These examples demonstrate that its passenger offering is described through named city pairs; they are not a complete inventory of Iranian intercity trains. Nor does a prominent route listing establish daily frequency or a seat available on a particular date. [s2]

The operator’s documented booking sequence begins with origin, destination, dates, passenger details, and accommodation choices, followed by available results and service information. It then proceeds through passenger identification, review, and payment. This sequence explains why a general route description and a dated reservation answer different questions. [s1]

content.heading: What remains to be established
content.content: A national comparison needs more than amenities and route advertising. It requires dated timetables, a verified operator inventory, and evidence about accessibility, reliability, and passenger volumes. None of those outcomes can be inferred from the marketing descriptions inspected here. This draft therefore explains how to interpret service information while leaving comparative judgments and current travel arrangements unresolved.
